title: Finance-tuned VADER as the default backend; FinBERT behind an extra
rationale: Stock VADER is actively wrong on market language, measured: 'Boeing recalls 200K units after safety probe launched' scored +0.51 (now -0.57); 'Tesla misses delivery estimates, shares slide 8%' scored +0.08 (now -0.78); 'Nvidia downgraded to underweight' scored 0.00 (now -0.84). The override needs no model download and drops ~2.5GB of torch from a default install, which was also what broke the virtualenv.

description: Multi-word entries added to VADER's lexicon never fire, because SentimentIntensityAnalyzer tokenises on whitespace. Every phrase in the lexicon ('cuts guidance', 'record high', 'profit warning') was dead weight, and the phrases matter most because some mean the OPPOSITE of their parts: 'dividend' is good news, 'cuts dividend' is not.
resolution: _collapse_phrases() rewrites known phrases to single underscored tokens before scoring, and the lexicon is keyed on the collapsed form. Verb/noun families that take a qualifier ('raises EARNINGS guidance', 'cuts ITS FULL-YEAR guidance') allow up to 3 intervening words; the rest stay strict, since loosening 'short seller' or 'profit taking' would invent signal. _resolve_phrase maps a matched span back to its lexicon key so qualifiers do not produce an unscored token.

description: Scoring title and description as one string flipped headlines positive: 'Rocket Lab (RKLB) Is Down 7.6% After Record US$266M Deal' scored +0.944, because the syndicated description was marketing copy ('find out what this record-breaking success means for you').
resolution: score_article() blends 75% title, 25% description. Descriptions from aggregators are frequently promotional, while the headline states the fact. Also added the direction words absent from stock VADER (down, up, higher, lower) since 'Is Down 7.6%' is the most common way a headline states the only thing that matters.
